question.problem:
What type of quadratic curve is defined by the following equation?

$$
{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}^{2}-4{x}_{2}=0
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we complete the squares for the variable ${x}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}^{2}-4{x}_{2} & =0 \\ {x}_{1}+2({x}_{2}^{2}-2{x}_{2}) & =0 \\ {x}_{1}+2({x}_{2}^{2}-2{x}_{2}+1-1) & =0 \\ {x}_{1}+2({x}_{2}-1)^{2}-2 & =0 \\ 2({x}_{2}-1)^{2} & =-({x}_{1}-2)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, performing the change of variables

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}={x}_{1}-2, \\ {y}_{2}={x}_{2}-1,\end{aligned}
$$

we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{y}_{2}^{2} & =-{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}^{2} & =-\frac{1}{2}{y}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

 

This represents a parabola that opens in the direction of the negative ${y}_{1}$-axis.
